question.worked_solution:
In the equation, $y$ is being *divided* by $3.$ To isolate $y$, we can perform the opposite operation, which is *multiplying* by $3.$ So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $3.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{3} & =-7 \\ 3\cdot \frac{y}{3} & =3\cdot (-7) \\ \frac{3y}{3} & =-21\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $3$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{3y}{3} & =-21 \\ \frac{\cancel{3}y}{\cancel{3}} & =-21 \\ y & =-21\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
